messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: py_var_context
parts:
Allen, is there a Cython equivalent of RList that would enable PyStan
to read in only what it needs to from the environment instead of putting
everything into the map<string, pair>? It’s no problem if not — the current
py_var_context should basically be subsumed by a C++ var_context that
will be defined in the api directly.

That's the usual story --- there's a very abstract base class
or concept, and then concrete implementations that deal with
messy issues like external storage.

For instance, ostream can write to sockets, files, strings in
memory, or anything else you can dream up. The key is that it
gives you a write method with certain properties.

messages.author: f4c2e63aec3c6db2
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] py_var_context
parts:
Interesting -- I thought PyStan was the same as R here.

In general, I'm in favor of subsuming. Cython will happily work with
simple C++ classes and standard data structures like vector and map.

Asking Cython to subclass a C++ class from elsewhere is trickier. For
example, I think the current py_var_context is written in C++ and not
Cython because of the need to subclass var_context_factory in
stan::interface.

If you get something working I'll try testing it. I still have that
branch somewhere where I tried to adapt to the new writer-callback
refactor.

Thanks,

Allen

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] py_var_context
parts:
Allen,

The big difference is in the internals. RStan uses an RList object internally which can be lazily queried for variables. CmdStan (dump.hpp) read in a text file, parses the parameters, and then stores everything in internal memory upon construction. PyStan parses all of the parameters into vectors externally and then passes them into the var context on construction.

Does Cython have an RList equivalent? Something that would wrap a dict and allow it to be queried lazily?

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] py_var_context
parts:
> Cython can definitely do what RStan does --- create something that
> exposes a dict-interface with lazy fetching.
>
> I might not be understanding the concern correctly -- but isn't delaying
> reading the data here a potentially bad thing? Isn't having an immutable
> version of the data a good thing?

Firstly I don’t think immutable var_contexts are going to be flexible
enough for every use case. I’m thinking in particular on the C++ side
where it’d be much easier to create a var context and then add data
one-by-one, a la

var_context context;
context.add_parameter(“name1”, values1, dims1);
context.add_parameter(“name2”, values2, dims2);
context.add_parameter(“name3”, values3, dims3);

Secondly, lazy querying is handy because users can add unnecessary
data into the source file/environment without incurring any I/O overhead.
For example, say someone wanted to put data, inits, and a metric all in
the same file. Lazy querying would allow us to create three different
var contexts using the same source but only load each parameter once
instead of in triplicate. Also this would open up the possibility of using
the local environment as a source instead of having to pass everything
in by hand.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] py_var_context
parts:
I don't think var_context itself should even have an implementation.
So some of the implementations can be just thin shells around
environments or dictionaries and we can also have a setter/getter
container like Michael's suggesting below.

In addition to what Michael said, the laziness only lasts until
data read time. At that point it gets read into the Stan model
object at construction time. This is the same point at which RStan
or CmdStan do validation, so there's no clean way to guarantee
behavior.

I just pasted the second response inline below.

> On Jun 24, 2015, at 7:18 AM, Michael Betancourt <betan...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Allen,
>
> The big difference is in the internals. RStan uses an RList object internally which can be lazily queried for variables.

That's in the future, right? Because now it'll balk if there's
other junk in the environment with NA values.

> CmdStan (dump.hpp) read in a text file, parses the parameters, and then stores everything in internal memory upon construction. PyStan parses all of the parameters into vectors externally and then passes them into the var context on construction.
>
> Does Cython have an RList equivalent? Something that would wrap a dict and allow it to be queried lazily?

Do we also want to wrap environments in Python? I'm happy
not doing that as it pollutes environments if they're global
as most people use these things.

Julia appears to have the same issues with C++ as Python, but
so far, Stan.jl is a wrapper around CmdStan rather than integrating
at the C++ level.

- Bob
